_note: Phase 3 VELA reconstruction workshop and return-mission simulation. SIMPLIFIED EDUCATIONAL GAMEPLAY MODEL: every component value, route requirement and constant here is invented for the game and is NOT NASA data. Units: mass kg, propellant kg, power W, energy Wh, time s, data MB, relay throughput MB/s, delta-v m/s.

recovered_components.name: Navigation Chip
recovered_components.note: Guides the rift transition and holds the base flight data store.

recovered_components.name: Power Core
recovered_components.note: Continuous electrical output plus a buffer for demand above that output.

recovered_components.name: Shield Emitter
recovered_components.note: Runs at idle until the debris-exposed transit, then at full power.

original_propulsion._note: The Phase 1 engine survives in the wreck and can be repaired. Keyed by the Phase 1 component id.

propulsion.name: Repair the original engine
propulsion.description: Cheap. Its performance is whatever you launched with on day one.

propulsion.name: Rebuilt Dawn cluster
propulsion.description: Rebuilt from Dawn Project stock: efficient and strong, but expensive to fabricate.

protection.name: Scrap armor plating
protection.description: +2 rating. Heavy, so it needs more propellant.

protection.name: Shield amplifier
protection.description: +2 rating. Light, but draws 90 W during the debris transit.

storage.name: Navigation chip store only
storage.description: 128 MB. Too small for the mandatory payload.

routes.name: Fast Corridor
routes.description: Short and violent: more delta-v, a dense debris field, and a short relay window.

routes.name: Extended Arc
routes.description: Long and quiet: less delta-v and light debris, but four hours of electrical load.
